thread:
jordan_acme: @support Hey — after the 03:10 deploy our p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.6s and we started seeing 500s. Stack traces in our app point at inference timeouts and some GPU OOM messages in the runtime logs. Can someone help triage? https://acme.logs/trace/ZXCV1234

emily_support: Sorry — that sounds bad. Which model and deployment? Is this Dedicated or Hosted? Any recent prompt/template changes?

jordan_acme: Model: redwood-open-13b-v2@rev-2026-03-16, deployment id dep-prod-44, Dedicated (us-west-2). We pushed a prompt change that increased max_tokens from 256 -> 1024 and started using long chat context. Sample request id: req_77b2a.

devon_support: Escalating to runtime oncall — @sam_oncall can you take a look? Adding logs snippet below I pulled from the runtime pod around the time of the spike.

sam_oncall: Got it, grabbing logs now. Initial glance: repeated OOMs and slow GC-like stalls, plus KV cache growth. Can you paste the runtime OOM snippet?

devon_support: Paste from pod runtime-gpu-3 at 2026-03-16T03:11:22Z:
```
[2026-03-16T03:11:22Z] ERROR runtime: alloc failed: GPU0: alloc 3.2G (requested) free 412M total 14.7G
[2026-03-16T03:11:22Z] WARN runtime: kv_cache items=1,248,372 -> growth after token bursts
[2026-03-16T03:11:23Z] WARN runtime: slab defrag triggered, reclaimed 64M but p99 stall 1.7s
[2026-03-16T03:11:25Z] ERROR api: request req_77b2a timed out -> 504
```

anya_ml_infra: That kv item count looks high for Dedicated per-worker defaults; long contexts + high concurrency = KV growth and fragmentation. Two paths: quick mitigations for customer, and longer-term allocator/kv limits.

emily_support: Jordan — can you temporarily rollback the prompt change to reduce max_tokens while we triage? Also please confirm concurrent request qps to that deployment.

jordan_acme: We can rollback, but need guidance on repro steps and any immediate runtime flags to flip. QPS is ~8 steady + occasional spikes to 20 during user bursts.

sam_oncall: Triage summary: likely cause = KV cache growth from longer contexts + higher concurrency -> allocator fragmentation and OOM/backpressure causing p99 spikes. Short-term mitigations you can try now (order matters):
1) rollback model prompt change or set max_tokens back to 256 (fast).
2) set per-request max_context_tokens (client-side) or server-side request limit: "max_new_tokens" lower.
3) reduce batch_size to 1 for that route and disable autoscaling bursts until stable.
4) temporarily disable local KV caching for that model: set header X-Redwood-KV-Cache: off (we can apply on your dedicated pool).
5) route a portion of traffic to a fallback smaller model (redwood-open-6b) while we stabilize.

Commands we can run if you want us to act: 
- Disable KV on pool: POST /v1/admin/pools/dep-prod-44/kv?enabled=false (auth admin)
- Temporarily pin to older model: POST /v1/deployments/dep-prod-44/rollout -> {
  "model": "redwood-open-13b-v1"
}
- Restart worker pod: kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/runtime-gpu-3

devon_support: We can apply the pool change and restart pods if you give us the go-ahead.

jordan_acme: Please disable KV for that pool and pin to redwood-open-13b-v1. We'll also rollback prompt. Do you want us to cut traffic?

sam_oncall: We'll do the pool change and a controlled rollout to older model + restart one pod to avoid simultaneous restarts. I'll also open internal ticket RUNTIME-423 to track allocator tuning and kv limits.

ops_bot: Action started: POST /admin/pools/dep-prod-44/kv -> disabled by devon_support at 3249991085
ops_bot: Action started: POST /deployments/dep-prod-44/rollout -> model pinned to redwood-open-13b-v1 by sam_oncall at 3249991120
ops_bot: Action started: kubectl rollout restart runtime-gpu-3 at 3249991180

sam_oncall: After the pool KV disable and restart, monitor p95/p99 and errors for ~5m. If p99 still >1s, we can throttle concurrency via per-route QPS limits.

jordan_acme: Rolling back prompt now, standing by.

[~6 minutes later]

emily_support: Jordan — any change in metrics?

jordan_acme: Good news — after rollback + pool change p99 down to ~480ms and 500s stopped. We'll keep traffic low while you investigate. Thanks.

sam_oncall: Great. Next steps (internal):
- RUNTIME-423: increase default kv eviction aggressiveness for Dedicated pools with long-context flags.
- Evaluate allocator tuning: consider larger initial free slabs and more aggressive defrag triggers.
- Add CV alert that ties kv_cache item-growth to p99 latency so future ops auto-alert.
- Add a per-deployment soft limit on KV items to avoid unbounded growth.

devon_support: I'll keep this thread updated and reach out once we have a patch or config change for Dedicated pools. Jordan, assigning a short maintenance window once we have a non-disruptive change.

jordan_acme: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast help. We'll reopen if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
